Playbook.name: Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Sent to a Personal / Public Email Domain - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Forcepoint DLP flagged sensitive-classified content (PCI / Sensitive Words-Outbound / Files Outbound) sent to a destination classified "Public Mail Domain" - typically an "Endpoint Email" send where the recipient list (cef.extensions.destinationUserName) mixes personal webmail (gmail / hotmail / yahoo / outlook) with internal or partner addresses. This is the single-event sibling of the bulk rule; triage: is a sensitive attachment genuinely leaving to a personal inbox, or is this a routine business email that also happens to CC a personal address?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Sending account-opening forms, passport copies, financial statements or PCI-scoped data to a personal inbox is a data-protection and PCI-DSS exposure for the bank, and a common insider / careless-handling pattern. Under Monitor Mode the mail is delivered, so the exposure is real once confirmed.

Assets.AssetType: Forcepoint DLP endpoints and email gateway (Endpoint Email / Content Gateway)

LogSources.LogSource: Forcepoint DLP CEF via syslog - logs-cef.log-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Forcepoint DLP CEF (verified live on logs-cef.log-*, observer.vendor == "Forcepoint"). Fields: cef.extensions.loginName (INTDOM\user), cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory (classification incl. "Public Mail Domain", "PCI", "Sensitive Words-Outbound", "Files Outbound"), cef.extensions.destinationUserName (recipient email list; on the email channel this is the true destination - destinationHosts is often "N/A"), cef.extensions.filename (attachment names and sizes), cef.extensions.deviceAction ("Permitted" / "Permitted, Monitor Mode" / "Blocked"), cef.extensions.sourceServiceName (channel: "Endpoint Email" vs web), cef.extensions.sourceHost (workstation), cef.extensions.eventId. Derived entity user.name = TO_LOWER(last token of loginName split on backslash).

Signal.Name: Sensitive Data Sent to a Personal / Public Email Domain
Signal.Details: Forcepoint DLP incident where the destination is a Public Mail Domain AND the content is classified PCI / Sensitive Words-Outbound / Files Outbound.

Input.name: $user
Input.description: Derived user.name = lowercased login without domain (e.g. katiaf). Matches the alert entity user.name (the sender).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Read the recipient list and the attachment names before judging - the classification alone is not the verdict.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact. A personal recipient + a genuinely sensitive attachment + permitted delivery is the concern.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether a genuinely sensitive attachment left to a personal / public inbox, or whether this is routine business mail incidentally classified.

Step.name: Summarise this user's sensitive-to-public-mail incidents
Step.Purpose: Count incidents, list recipients, categories, channels and action for the sender in the window.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Public Mail Domain*" AND (cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Sensitive Words-Outbound*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Files Outbound*") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL user.name = TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))) | WHERE user.name == "$user" | STATS incidents = COUNT(*), recipients = VALUES(cef.extensions.destinationUserName), categories = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory), actions = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceAction), channels = VALUES(cef.extensions.sourceServiceName), hosts = VALUES(cef.extensions.sourceHost) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: One incident to a single personal recipient can still be a real leak if the attachment is sensitive. Many incidents / many personal recipients raises this toward the bulk-exfil playbook (PB-JCB-NEW-1).

Step.name: Enumerate each send: recipients, attachments, action
Step.Purpose: Show the concrete evidence - who received what file, on which channel, permitted or blocked.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Public Mail Domain*" AND (cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Sensitive Words-Outbound*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Files Outbound*") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL user.name = TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))) | WHERE user.name == "$user" | KEEP @timestamp, cef.extensions.destinationUserName, cef.extensions.destinationHosts, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory, cef.extensions.deviceAction, cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.sourceServiceName, cef.extensions.sourceHost, cef.extensions.eventId | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: Read the recipient list: internal / known-partner addresses only = likely routine. A personal webmail address receiving a sensitive attachment = the leak. Read the filename: account-opening forms, passports, statements are genuinely sensitive; embedded signature images (image001.jpg) are not.

Step.name: Confirm delivery to a genuinely personal inbox
Step.Purpose: Isolate the sends whose recipient list actually contains a personal webmail domain - the decisive evidence, filtering out partner-only business mail.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Public Mail Domain*" AND (cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Sensitive Words-Outbound*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Files Outbound*") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL user.name = TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))) | WHERE user.name == "$user" | EVAL rcpt = TO_LOWER(cef.extensions.destinationUserName) | WHERE rcpt LIKE "*gmail*" OR rcpt LIKE "*hotmail*" OR rcpt LIKE "*yahoo*" OR rcpt LIKE "*outlook*" OR rcpt LIKE "*proton*" OR rcpt LIKE "*icloud*" | KEEP @timestamp, cef.extensions.destinationUserName, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory, cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.deviceAction | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Rows here = sensitive content confirmed to a personal inbox. Zero rows = the "Public Mail Domain" classification did not resolve to a genuine personal recipient in the recipient list (lean towards misconfiguration / benign). Extend the domain list if the org sees other personal providers.

Node.Condition: A genuinely sensitive attachment (PCI / account form / passport / statement) was permitted to a personal webmail recipient (INV-03 returns rows).
Node.Result: True Positive (Sensitive Data to Personal Email - data-handling / possible exfiltration)

Node.Condition: Forcepoint Blocked the send, OR the recipients are all internal / approved-partner addresses and the transfer is business-justified.
Node.Result: False Positive (Authorised business mail or proven blocked by policy)

Node.Condition: The "Public Mail Domain" or sensitivity classification is a false match (e.g. only embedded signature images, or a partner domain mislabeled), with no real personal recipient.
Attachment sensitivity or recipient legitimacy cannot be determined from the logs alone.
Node.Result: Needs Escalation (data-handling review with the sender's manager)

FalsePositive.Definition: Authorised business mail, or a send that Forcepoint proved it Blocked.

Indicators.Item: Recipients are internal or approved-partner domains only.
Business justification exists for the send.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the recipients / justification or the block outcome; document; close as authorised_or_blocked (not "benign").

TruePositive.Definition: A sensitive attachment reached a personal / public inbox.

Indicators.Item: Genuinely sensitive attachment (PCI / forms / IDs / statements).

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the content with DLP / compliance; interview the sender; assess whether it was error or intent; if a pattern or intent, escalate to the bulk-exfil workflow and open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: Classification false match - no genuine personal recipient or no genuine sensitive content.

Indicators.Item: Partner domain mislabeled as public mail.

SOCAction.Item: Raise a DLP classification-tuning request; document; suppress the specific benign match.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Read the recipient list and attachment names; determine whether a personal inbox received genuinely sensitive content and whether the send was permitted or blocked.
If a sensitive attachment was permitted to a personal inbox, preserve the incident record and engage DLP / compliance.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Review the attachment content with compliance; interview the sender to establish intent vs error; if intentional or repeated, restrict the account and escalate to IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Consider Block mode for sensitive categories to personal-mail destinations; reinforce data-handling training for the individual / team; tune classification to cut false matches.

Escalation.Trigger: A genuinely sensitive attachment confirmed permitted to a personal inbox, a repeated pattern by the same sender, or any indication of intent or account compromise.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Recipients / justification or block outcome confirmed and documented; classification false-match (if any) raised for tuning.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Content reviewed with compliance; sender addressed; intent vs error established; controls tightened; case recorded (IR opened if intentional / repeated).
